Direct seated vs prone leg curl training study. Twenty healthy adults, no systematic resistance training in the prior 12 months, trained one leg seated and the other prone for 12 weeks at 70% 1RM after ramp-up, 10 reps x 5 sets twice weekly; MRI measured individual and whole hamstring volumes. Seated condition used a modified Life Fitness seated leg curl with hip around 90 degrees, knee ROM 0-90 degrees, pelvis strapped, and settings repeated.

Close direct modified seated leg-curl evidence. Forty-two healthy young males completed 34 sessions over 12 weeks or served as controls. Lengthened-state eccentric training used isoinertial weight-stack resistance in an accentuated hip-flexed seated-curl setup; MRI measured seven knee-flexor volumes and biceps femoris long-head aponeurosis, and torque/EMG were measured during maximum knee-flexion contractions.

Leg-curl movement-family EMG. Eleven weight-trained men performed leg curl, stiff-leg deadlift, and back squat at 75% 1RM for hamstring EMG comparison. Used only to support hamstring involvement in loaded leg curls, not seated-machine specificity.

Fine-wire EMG during maximum knee flexion. Ten healthy subjects performed isometric and isokinetic knee flexion; semitendinosus, semimembranosus, biceps femoris long head, and biceps femoris short head were measured. Used for individual hamstring knee-flexion role and joint-angle limitations.

Gastrocnemius in leg-curl-like knee flexion. Nine healthy men performed maximum isokinetic knee flexion at 30, 75, and 150 degrees/s with ankle braced in dorsiflexion or plantar flexion; knee moment was higher with the ankle dorsiflexed. Used for gastrocnemius secondary role and ankle-position limitation.

excludedSources.title: Tsaklis et al. 2015 muscle and intensity based hamstring exercise classification
excludedSources.reason: Reviewed as hamstring EMG context, but the described curl was a standing elastic-band knee-flexion/hip-extension task in elite female track athletes, not the assigned seated machine variant.

excludedSources.title: McAllister et al. 2014 Muscle Activation During Various Hamstring Exercises
excludedSources.reason: Relevant prone leg-curl and hamstring-exercise EMG family evidence, but not used because direct seated MRI evidence plus older leg-curl EMG and knee-flexion fine-wire EMG were sufficient for the visible roles.

notes: Variant assumption: a seated hamstring curl machine with the thighs restrained and resistance applied through a lower-leg pad during knee flexion. Direct exact-variant EMG for generic commercial seated leg curl machines was not found; the primary hamstring role is based on direct seated-machine MRI training evidence plus close loaded leg-curl and maximum knee-flexion EMG. Gastrocnemius is visible only as secondary because its contribution is ankle-position dependent and not the intended target. Sartorius, gracilis, popliteus, and individual hamstring heads were not shown separately because the evidence did not support clean app roles for a generic machine card. No support muscles were added because the machine supplies most external stability and reviewed sources did not identify a specific stabilizer role. Current shared anatomy assets include local BodyParts3D hamstrings and gastrocnemius meshes for this movement.
